clue.text: Final instructions I'm following for prince or king

indicators.note: following says the words I'm come after the final instructions in the answer

parts.note: a will holds a person's last instructions, for after death
I'm is short for I AM

explanation.surface: Someone takes their last orders, then names a royal heir.
explanation.definitionFit: William is the name of a current prince and of several English kings, so a fair example.

clue.text: Royal vow about Irish oddball

indicators.note: about means the royal vow wraps around the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: a monarch uses the royal 'we', so the wedding vow 'I do' becomes 'we do'

explanation.surface: A monarch's promise is made about some eccentric Irish character.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we' turns the marriage vow 'I do' into WE DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is a strange, eccentric person, a straight synonym for an oddball.

clue.text: Communicate part of regalia is Edwardian

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Talking about crown jewels dating from the Edwardian era.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in contact and cooperate, which is to communicate with another party.

clue.text: Moorish prince oddly represented in same structure

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh form
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word prince

explanation.surface: A Moorish ruler, portrayed in an unusual way, is shown in a matching shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives PIC from prince; 'represented' shuffles MOORISH plus PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomorphic, from Greek for equal form, describes things having the same structure or shape.

clue.text: Silently reflected unlike Victoria, famously losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not amused', so one unlike her is entertained

explanation.surface: Someone thought quietly, not at all like the famously stony old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We are not amused' is the line attributed to Queen Victoria; dropping the A of AMUSED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or meditate quietly, so the past tense matches thinking things over in silence.

clue.text: Put in charge by king or queen in spot where mace etc are kept

indicators.note: in means the joined letters are placed inside the word for spot

parts.note: to spot something is to see or spy it

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the monarch's letters sit just after the charge letters

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina, Edward Rex) is a monarch's cipher, fitting a king or queen

explanation.surface: Appointed to oversee, by the monarch, the place where the ceremonial mace lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' simply instructs; the mace here is the spice, not the ceremonial staff the royal theme suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicery is a storeroom for spices, and mace is a spice made from nutmeg husks.

clue.text: Like evil so-called prince, a last Inca butchered

indicators.note: butchered means hacked about, so these letters are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A wicked figure styled a prince slaughters the final Inca ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Satan is called the Prince of Darkness, hence the 'so-called prince'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanical means of or like Satan, the devil traditionally titled the Prince of Darkness.

clue.text: Flag man honoured by monarch and I hoisted

indicators.note: hoisted means raised up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a knighted man is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A knighted man and I run up a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but the plant also called a yellow flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild species of iris, and flag is a common name for many irises.

clue.text: With prince, he revised code

indicators.note: revised means altered and reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: He and a prince together rewrote a code of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'code' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher is to put a message into cipher, that is, to encode it.

clue.text: English paper royal couple turned up in Californian park

indicators.note: turned up means flipped upwards, so in this down entry the letters read backwards

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper
a couple of letters taken from the heart of the word royal

explanation.surface: An English newspaper's royal pair surface in a Californian park.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a London newspaper; the 'royal couple' is the pair of letters in the middle of 'royal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is the famous national park in the Sierra Nevada of California.

clue.text: Villain dramatically trapping male monarch, say, finally

indicators.note: trapping means the villain's name encloses the male letter

parts.note: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello, a stage villain

explanation.surface: A stage villain ensnares a male king at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is the butterfly, and the imago is its final, adult stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the last, fully adult stage of an insect such as a monarch butterfly.

clue.text: Eg king and queen making formal speeches

definitions.meaning: a king and queen are among the pieces in a chess set
prepared, rehearsed orations delivered on a grand occasion

explanation.surface: A royal couple delivering ceremonial addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces from a set fit the first sense; a set piece is also a carefully prepared formal address.

clue.text: Duke upset person (not king) with depression, in low spirits

indicators.note: with says the depression comes along next, added on the end
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says the king's letter is to be dropped from the word person

parts.note: R (Rex) is the standard abbreviation for king
a dent is a small hollow or depression in a surface

explanation.surface: A disgruntled duke, no longer royal, sinks into a gloomy state.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not king)' removes R from PERSON; 'upset' shuffles the remaining PESON into ESPON.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondent means dejected and without hope, the same as feeling down.

clue.text: Unwanted messages monarch's opening after spring

indicators.note: after puts the monarch's letter behind the spring in the answer

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: opening means the very start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Junk mail arrives after the king opens his inbox in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the name for unsolicited bulk email, junk that nobody wants.

clue.text: How crowning moment arrives? You, we hear, may tell it otherwise

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that is spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: the word you said aloud is the letter U

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A puzzled listener is told the tale of a coronation might be told differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crowning moment' is the climax, which comes at the end; the ? flags that playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimately means in the end, and a crowning moment, the culmination, is what comes last.

clue.text: Extremely lavish directions in information for buyers

indicators.note: in means the direction letters are placed within the buyers' information

parts.note: a price list tells shoppers what goods cost
N and E stand for the compass directions north and east
a price list tells shoppers what goods cost
N and E stand for the compass directions north and east
a price list tells shoppers what goods cost

explanation.surface: Instructions printed inside a sales brochure describing the most luxurious goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' gives two compass points, north and east, and each is slipped into a different word of PRICE LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Princely means magnificent or lavish, so the superlative is the most lavish of all.

clue.text: Performing part of coronation that could make money

definitions.meaning: carrying out the formal installing of a monarch in office, part of the crowning
putting funds into stocks or property in hope of profit

explanation.surface: The ceremonial bit of crowning a king that might turn a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to install formally in an office, as at a coronation, and also to put money to work.

clue.text: Jewels from Queen pocketed by damsel in distress?

indicators.note: pocketed by means the queen's letters are tucked inside the other letters
in distress means troubled and disordered, so the word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Gems taken from a queen and hidden away by a damsel in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' scrambles DAMSEL to make EMALDS, which then holds ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green precious gemstones, so they are jewels.

clue.text: Conservative old boy included in excellent royal award

indicators.note: included in means these letters are placed inside the word for excellent

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A Tory former schoolboy receives a fine honour from the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The accolade was the tap of the sword in knighthood, and the word now means any honour or award.

clue.text: Writer about prince using computer I have changed, returned with complaint

indicators.note: with says the following piece is added on next

parts.note: Mac is the Apple Macintosh computer

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a new order
returned means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a complaint is an illness, something one is ill with

explanation.surface: A biographer of a prince, working on a computer, sends back a grumbling revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns I HAVE into HIAVE; 'returned' turns ILL into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli wrote The Prince, the Renaissance treatise on how a ruler holds power.

clue.text: What's satisfying about one answer, like Cordelia's response to Lear

indicators.note: about means the satisfying word goes around the other letters

parts.note: one's fill is a satisfying amount
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something satisfying about a reply, much as the loyal daughter spoke to her old king.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Cordelia is the daughter who answers her father with honest duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Filial means befitting a son or daughter, as Cordelia's dutiful reply to her father is.

clue.text: Like crowned head lying, hard?

definitions.meaning: from Shakespeare's line about a crowned head resting with no peace of mind
read as ..., the opposite of easy, that is, difficult

explanation.surface: A worried king lying awake asks if his lot is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry IV says 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown'; the ? flags reading the word as not-easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation gives anxious; split as a negative, the same word means not easy, difficult.

clue.text: Cheat man most removed in rank from king or queen

definitions.text: man most removed in rank from king or queen
definitions.meaning: a chess piece that starts in the corner square, as far along the back row from the royal pair as possible

explanation.surface: A trickster is a man of very low status compared with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' is the chess row, not social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle, and the rook is the chessman starting at the end of the back rank.

clue.text: I turn up so disturbed about a dethronement, possibly

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the single letter
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows up, upset, to talk of overthrowing a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles I TURN UP SO into USURPTION, which goes around the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpation is the wrongful seizing of power, which may involve deposing a monarch.

clue.text: One often on tabloid page? This is bigger than that

definitions.text: One often on tabloid page? This is bigger than that

parts.words: One often on tabloid page? This is bigger than that
parts.note: members of the monarch's family fill the popular press, and the same word names a paper size larger than tabloid

explanation.surface: A celebrity regularly in the papers is compared in size with the paper itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tabloid' is both the newspaper type and a page size; the answer is also a traditional paper size that is larger.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the crown's family are tabloid staples, and royal is a printing paper size larger than tabloid.

clue.text: Help a princess on stage

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Assist a princess appearing in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is the Ethiopian princess who is the heroine of Verdi's opera.

clue.text: Disadvantage in wobbliness about word ER avoids?

indicators.note: about means the word for wobbliness goes around the avoided word

parts.note: lability is instability, a tendency to wobble or change
the Queen uses the royal 'we' instead of the first-person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: The problem with shakiness is the word the Queen won't use.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; using the royal 'we', she avoids saying I.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a drawback or handicap, something that puts one at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Henry's protege having Tudor name, up to a point

indicators.note: up to a point means only partway, so the name is cut short and its end dropped

parts.note: Elizabeth I was the last Tudor monarch

explanation.surface: A man's young pupil bears a Tudor queen's name, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is Professor Henry Higgins of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, who coaches Eliza Doolittle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl Henry Higgins takes on and trains in speech.

clue.text: Queen's location once, no good situation

parts.note: the biblical Queen of Sheba ruled the ancient kingdom of Sheba

explanation.surface: Where a queen once lived is now in a bad state.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang, as in 'the whole shebang', means an affair or matter, a situation in general.

clue.text: What devoted followers show ruling family initially changing side

indicators.note: the first letter, the right-hand mark, is switched to the left-hand one, a change of side

parts.note: royalty is the royal family, those who rule

explanation.surface: Devoted subjects stick by the crown even when changing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are right and left, so the first letter swaps side.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is steadfast faithfulness, the quality committed supporters display.
